decoys.description: 0.0.0.0/0 opened then reverted to internal within 2h in dev
decoys.note: The open fires T1562.007 because the stateless detector sees a world-open source range. The 2h revert is a separate event; a stateless detector cannot correlate the pair. Distinguishing benign short-lived changes from malicious ones requires an allowlist or temporal-correlation layer, which is out of the current three-surface scope.

decoys.description: Approved read-only external viewer in staging
decoys.note: The grant to approved-external-viewer@trusted-vendor.example.com fires T1199 because the identity is non-corp and non-SA. It is an approved partner grant; distinguishing approved external partners from malicious external identities requires an allowlist, which is out of the current three-surface scope.

staging-owner-sa@fake-staging-002 is granted roles/owner in staging as part of normal deploy automation. It fires T1098.003 because roles/owner is a high-privilege role. Distinguishing expected deploy SAs from malicious high-privilege grants requires an allowlist or behavioral baseline, which is out of the current three-surface scope.
